executive_assessment.text: The release reports 2015–16 drought affected 18 of Cambodia’s 25 provinces and over 2.5 million people.
The release estimates 2019 El Niño drought-related rice-production losses at US$100 million.
NDC 3.0 sets out climate-risk assessment and inclusive, climate-resilient WASH frameworks and provincial action plans for all 25 provinces, with a 2035 target.

geographic_notes.text: 14 provinces in Cambodia: The release says September 2022 rainfall flooded 14 provinces, affecting about 85,000 households; landslides prompted 5,000 household evacuations.

Cambodia; southern plains: NDC 3.0 reports major floods recur about every five years, severe agricultural drought has a 4% median annual probability, and the southern plains face severe drought roughly every five to six years.

Mekong River region; Tonle Sap Basin; northwest Cambodia: The NDC identifies low-income households along the Mekong, Tonle Sap Basin, and northwest Cambodia as disproportionately exposed to floods, drought, and heat, with risks to agricultural livelihoods.
Cambodia; 25 provinces: NDC 3.0 sets out climate-risk assessment and inclusive, climate-resilient WASH frameworks and provincial action plans for all 25 provinces, with a 2035 target.

known_gaps.text: No inspected source explicitly links climate hazards to conflict or violence; no country-specific climate-FCV pathway is asserted.
NDC hazard and vulnerability estimates rely partly on cited secondary studies; underlying methods were not separately assessed.
NDC WASH commitments and targets are plans, not evidence of implementation or service outcomes.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
